added_findings.title: VV-only folder-50 integrations TV never wired: keep them through every host-file port
added_findings.detail:
VV wires four integrations of folder 50 that TV's realign plan s.9.3 lists but TV's code lacks:
(1) 30/Na__UiFeature__ImageExport__Controls.js:53, 295, 330 composites the projected-linework vectors onto image exports of a drawing (Na__PlExport__Apply). TV's image export never calls it, so TV's ExportCompositor is dead code.
(2) 01/Na__AppFlow__LoadingSequence.js:435, 1327 calls Na__PlOverlay__SyncFrame on every drawing frame. Nothing in TV calls it per frame, although TV's SvgOverlay says 'call every frame', so TV's on-screen overlay is registered only on Paint/SetShown (not observed at runtime).
(3) 43/Na__FloorPlan__DevMenu__Editor__.js:122, 577 and 46/Na__Elevation__DevMenu__Editor__.js:111, 711 bake linework before the drawings save (D20). TV defines BakeBeforeSave but never calls it.
(4) 26/Na__UiFeature__ModelToggle__Controls.js:178 dispatches na-model-visibility-changed. Both apps' Pipeline (VV :663, TV :731) and SnapshotRenderer listen for it, but TV never dispatches it.
A swarm task that takes a TV version of any of these host files (S02a's dev editor ports, S09's LoadingSequence seams, an image-export port, a ModelToggle port) would silently delete working VV behaviour.
added_findings.recommendation: Mark all four as keep_vv_divergence in the ledger and in each host file's PORT NOTE. Add a grep check to the acceptance of every package that touches 30 ImageExport Controls, 01 LoadingSequence, the 43/46 DevMenu Editors or 26 ModelToggle Controls: Na__PlExport__Apply, Na__PlOverlay__SyncFrame, Na__PlStore__BakeBeforeSave and 'na-model-visibility-changed' must still be present. On the TV side (Adam's approval) they are back-port candidates: (4) is already in WP-S09-14, (3) is S02a's D-S02a-02, and (1) and (2) can be offered in the same TV session (WP-S02b-10R item 4).
added_findings.evidence: Importer map (verify_s02b/importers.py): TV has no importer of ExportCompositor, of Persistence BakeBeforeSave or of SvgOverlay SyncFrame outside folder 50. A grep of TV 02__Src__AppModules for 'na-model-visibility-changed' finds listeners only (Pipeline :156/:731, SnapshotRenderer :420). TV realign plan s.9.3 (integration edits). VV ledger Phase 4 last three rows.

added_findings.title: Depth fog and projected vectors: on screen neither app fogs the SVG overlay; VV exports put vectors above the fog
added_findings.detail:
The fog layer draws into the WebGL canvas. On screen, the projected linework is a DOM SVG overlay above the canvas in both apps (Na__PlOverlay__Paint from both Pipelines, TV :306, VV :264). So on screen the fog fades surfaces, fat SketchUp lines and profile lines, but never the projected vectors; TV behaves the same. On sheets the fog image sits above div.linework, so vectors are fogged there (TV B10).
VV-only: Na__PlExport__Apply draws the vectors onto every image export of a drawing AFTER the raster (30/...ImageExport__Controls.js:295, 330). A per-tile fog therefore lies under them, and vectors behind the plane print unfogged. TV's image export carries no vectors, so TV gives no reference.
WP-S02b-04's acceptance line ('projected vectors behind the plane fade') is true only for sheets.
added_findings.recommendation: Correct the WP-S02b-04 acceptance (done in WP-S02b-04R). Ask Adam (D-S02b-V02) whether VV image exports should match sheets. If yes, render a fog-only layer through the tiled path (Na__ElevFog__RenderLayerFrame) and composite it AFTER Na__PlExport__Apply. If no, document that vectors stay crisp in exports.
added_findings.evidence: VV 50/...ExportCompositor__.js:87-104; VV 30/...ImageExport__Controls.js:295, 330; TV 30 ImageExport Controls imports (no PlExport); TV fog plan s.3.3 and row B10; TV Pipeline :306, VV Pipeline :264

added_decisions.question: Which gate should control VV's linework bake (Na__PlStore__BakeBeforeSave)? This replaces D-S02b-06.
added_decisions.options: a) Na__DevGate__IsAuthoringEnabled(), as TV (TD01); b) keep Na__AppUtils__IsRunningOnLocalhost() (VV's data-path rule)
added_decisions.recommendation: b). VV's DevGate is defined to leave data-path writes on the hostname test, because VV's writes need Flask (/api/editor-config, then the mirror). VV's LE asset gate follows the same rule. a) would let an unlocked session outside localhost render every drawing and then fail the upload.

added_decisions.question: SnapshotHistory file name: which app renames? D-S02b-12 and WP-S09-10 disagree.
added_decisions.options: a) VV renames to TV's Na__AppUtils__SnapshotHistory.js (WP-S09-10); b) TV renames to the house __ convention (D-S02b-12)
added_decisions.recommendation: a), delivered by WP-S09-10. The goal is VV aligned to TV, and only two importers exist in each app. b) is an optional TV house-style tidy. Schedule exactly one.

added_decisions.question: VV image exports composite the projected-linework vectors AFTER the raster (Na__PlExport__Apply, VV-only), so a per-tile depth fog lies under them. Should exports match sheets, where the fog sits above the vectors?

added_decisions.recommendation: b) if Adam wants exports to read like sheets, otherwise a). TV has no reference, because its image export carries no projected vectors.

notes:
The S02b survey is high quality. Its file inventory, code-level drift table and per-version deltas held up under an independent comment-stripped re-diff of all 48 shared files and every 'VV lacks' search; no finding was refuted outright. Its strongest claim, that the door module must land first, was proven at link level: a scratch simulation running VV's own exports verifier shows exactly 7 DoorPose names unresolved without the merge, and 4 Video Studio names lost with a verbatim TV copy. Note: the replacement WPs carry over the original 'Na__Test__FlushJoins__ passes 8/8' wording, but that is the TV assertion count; the TV script prints 8 PASS lines but counts some check() calls with multiple assertions, so the planner should treat 'exits 0' as the gate, not the literal 8.

Corrections the planner must apply:
- F28 / D-S02b-06 is reversed. VV's DevGate deliberately keeps data-path writes on localhost, so Persistence needs no code change at all; TV's version would not even link in VV.
- F42's export-hook spec would have drawn the section overlay twice per tile.
- WP-S02b-04's acceptance expected projected vectors to fade on screen and in exports. They cannot: the on-screen overlay is a DOM SVG in both apps, and VV composites export vectors after the raster.

Watch-outs:
(1) This slice overlaps S02a, S04a, S06b and S09 heavily, with two direct conflicts: D-S02a-01's renumber versus F01, and WP-S09-10's SnapshotHistory rename versus D-S02b-12. Resolve S02b-V03 / D-S02b-V03 before dispatch.
(2) Four VV-only linework integrations (S02b-V01) will be silently deleted by any whole-file TV port of their host files unless the acceptance greps are added.
(3) TV's own StoreyBand test is red because of the ConfigAccess fallback token, so a verbatim ConfigAccess copy fails in VV too.
(4) The tests carry NA project names (RB05 West Farm) that need neutral labels in the Vale repo.

Still unverified: runtime behaviour, and whether Vale models carry tags 76-79, Storey__ groups with doors, or Linetype door swings. Scratch artefacts are in scratchpad/parity/verify_s02b/; the report was edited in place, and a backup of the original is in verify_s02b.
